Jev-Urdu is Muhammad Noman's Urdu-first decision model with a multilingual mmBERT-base encoder and a decision head. Reported evaluation covers independent Urdu and Roman Urdu benchmarks, with mixed Urdu-English evaluated in a narrow internal workflow harness. English prompts change question and option language, not passage language. Full-suite results, matched API samples, batch throughput, and calibration limitations are documented separately in the launch article. Further-language performance is not established by this release. The jev-urdu 0.1.0 Python library is published on PyPI at https://pypi.org/project/jev-urdu/0.1.0/ (Python 3.10+); install with python -m pip install jev-urdu==0.1.0, import jev_urdu, then call jev_urdu.load(). Library documentation: https://huggingface.co/muhammadnoman76/jev-urdu/blob/main/library/README.md. The library downloads and caches the separately published model when loaded.

MakeItColor is Muhammad Noman's free Windows app ("Black-and-white photos and videos, in colour and restored. On your own PC."), version 1.0.0, released 20 October 2026. It colours photos (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, GIF, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, JPEG XR) and videos (MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, WMV, WebM, MPEG, M2TS/TS, FLV, 3GP, OGV, VOB, MXF). The colour model is the MakeItColor model on Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/muhammadnoman76/makeitcolor), based on DDColor (ConvNeXt-L; Kang et al., ICCV 2023; Apache 2.0) and converted to ONNX: it works on the picture's lightness at 512 x 512 and predicts the two colour channels, which are enlarged to full size, lined up with the edges by a guided filter and combined with the full-size lightness, so full resolution is kept. Photos get a before/after view with a draggable divider, a colour strength slider (50-150 %) and are saved as new files (PNG lossless or JPEG quality 95, name (color).png); originals are never changed. Fix brightness and contrast (on by default) is an automatic levels stretch (darkest and brightest 0.5 %, at most 1.8x, never less contrast); in videos it follows each shot slowly and matches each frame's brightness to the three frames before and after it, which removes film flicker. Enhance photos (on by default) uses Real-ESRGAN's compact general model (realesr-general-x4v3 blended 50/50 with its weak-denoise twin; BSD 3-Clause) to remove blur, noise and JPEG damage, in 256 x 256 tiles; Auto makes photos under 2000 px 2x or 4x larger, up to 24 megapixels. The colour model never sees the enhanced picture (in a first version it did and the colours changed). Videos come out as H.264 MP4 at the original size and frame rate with the original sound; Steady colours (on by default) keeps colours where the picture doesn't change and halved colour flicker on a 600-frame test clip (5.40 to 2.76); Clean up videos is Full (the enhancer on every frame at up to 800 px, detail kept steady where nothing moves), Light or Off, with Auto choosing Full on an NPU or graphics card and Light on the CPU. Both models run through Windows ML (ONNX Runtime): NPU first, then the best graphics card, then the CPU, and every chip is checked with a known test picture against the float32 CPU result before use. Measured on the author's laptop (Intel Core Ultra 5 135U): one 512 x 512 colour pass takes 0.41-0.42 s on the Intel AI Boost NPU and 1.8-2.4 s on the CPU; a 1500 x 1000 photo enhanced to 3000 x 2000 and coloured takes about 3 s with the enhancer on the graphics card and about 50 s on the CPU alone; a 1280 x 720 film colours at about 1.5 frames a second with Full clean-up. The first time, the Intel NPU needs about 4-5 minutes to compile the colour model. The colour model downloads on first use (456 MB float16 for NPU/GPU, 912 MB float32 for the CPU, SHA-256 checked); the enhancer ships with the app. Its colours are the model's best guess, not a record: skies, skin and grass usually come out right, clothes, cars and painted walls are a guess, dark shots can get a colour cast, moving things can change colour within a shot, and at 4x fine textures can look slightly painted. Two installers, hosted as GitHub release assets: Windows 10 (1903 or later) and 11, x64 and ARM64 (self-contained .NET 10); there is no 32-bit or Windows 7/8.1 build (no Windows ML there). It updates itself from https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/makeitcolor.json. It uses FFmpeg (LGPL 2.1) and is not affiliated with the DDColor or Real-ESRGAN authors. The app images on this site are real screenshots rendered by the app's own capture mode, and the before/after pictures are real output, using stills of the film Doraha (1967) and the title card of the public-domain film Duck and Cover (1951); the launch video uses short excerpts of Doraha and its song, "Tumhain Kaisay Bata Dun" (sung by Ahmad Rushdi), as its soundtrack. Not tested: ARM64 hardware, AMD and Qualcomm NPUs, NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, and Windows 10 itself.

PawSip is Muhammad Noman's free Windows water-reminder app with an animated vector cat companion and desktop widget. Reminders follow the user's presence (screen on, unlocked, recent keyboard or mouse input), wait during fullscreen apps, and repeat every 15 minutes until a drink is logged. Version 1.0.2 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). Data stays on the PC. From 1.0.2 it updates itself: about 30 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads the JSON feed at https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/pawsip.json (an ordinary HTTPS request; nothing else is sent), offers a newer version on its dashboard or with a tray notification that waits while a fullscreen app runs, and on Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256, installs it silently for the current user and starts again in the tray. The check can be turned off in Settings › Updates. Resource figures in the article were measured on the author's Windows 11 PC; the ARM64 and Windows 7 builds were not tested on their native hardware.

VibePlayer is Muhammad Noman's free Windows media player with a YouTube-style interface, written in C# with WPF on LibVLC 3.0.24 (the engine inside VLC media player, used under the LGPL; VibePlayer is not affiliated with VideoLAN). Its skip mode lets the user mark parts of a video, by typing start and end times or pressing [ and ] while watching; the player jumps over those parts every time that file plays, checking the position every 40 ms. Marks are stored per file in the app's settings (%APPDATA%\VibePlayer) and the video file is never modified; skips apply to local files, not network streams. It opens 47 video and 34 audio file types. Version 1.0.2 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). From 1.0.2 it updates itself: shortly after start-up and at most once a day it reads the JSON feed at https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/vibeplayer.json (an ordinary HTTPS request; nothing else is sent), offers a newer version in a non-modal card, and on Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256, installs it silently in place and restarts. The check can be turned off in Settings › Updates. The VibePlayer images and launch video on this site are recreations of the app's interface composited with Big Buck Bunny footage (© 2008 Blender Foundation, CC BY 3.0), not screenshots. The ARM64 build was not run on ARM hardware, and no build was run on an actual Windows 7 or 8.1 machine.

VibeVideo AI is a separate, free preview (version 0.1.0, 18 October 2026) of Muhammad Noman's VibePlayer with an AI scene filter that runs on the user's PC. While a local video plays it samples two pictures per second (from the playback position first, then the rest), scores each with OpenAI's CLIP ViT-B/32 image encoder (MIT) against 46 short text descriptions (kissing, sex scenes, nudity and ordinary scenes), turns runs of high scores into scenes (two frames over the threshold or one far over it, nearby scenes merged, edges snapped to shot cuts or padded), marks them in pink on the progress bar and jumps over them during playback. The user chooses nudity and sex and/or kissing, Low/Medium/High sensitivity (no rescan needed), the processor (Auto: NPU, then GPU via DirectML, then CPU, through Windows ML), and controls every scene in a Scenes to skip window that lists the AI's scenes (pink) and the user's own (amber) with their times: keep or skip each AI scene, move any scene's start and end a second at a time or by typing, watch a scene once without skipping it, put an AI scene back to the AI's times, and add scenes the AI missed. These choices are saved per file with the scan and are matched to the scene again after a rescan, a sensitivity change or switching the extra detector. An optional extra nudity detector, NudeNet 320n (AGPL-3.0), is off by default and downloads only when switched on. The CLIP model (176 MB 16-bit for NPU/GPU, 352 MB 32-bit for CPU) downloads on first use and is SHA-256 checked; videos are never uploaded or modified, and scans are cached per file in %LOCALAPPDATA%\VibeVideoAI\scans. On the author's laptop (Intel Core Ultra 5 135U) a 2-minute 1080p clip scanned at about 17x real time on the Intel AI Boost NPU. It is an early preview: it can miss scenes and mark harmless ones (at High sensitivity it marked five seconds of the 1951 film Duck and Cover as nudity or sex), it is not parental control, and it does not scan network streams. Two installers: Windows 10 (1903 or later) and 11, x64 and ARM64 (self-contained .NET 10); there is no 32-bit or Windows 7/8.1 build. It updates itself from https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/vibevideo-ai.json and installs beside VibePlayer, not over it. Not tested: ARM64 hardware, AMD and Qualcomm NPUs, discrete GPUs and Windows 10. The images and launch video of VibeVideo AI on this site recreate its interface from its source with public-domain footage (Duck and Cover, 1951; The Kiss, 1896; Kissing the War Goodbye, 1945); the scene times and frame scores shown are from the app's real scan.

Trove is Muhammad Noman's free archive manager for Windows, written in C# with WPF on the official, unmodified 7z.dll from 7-Zip 26.04 (used under the GNU LGPL with the unRAR licence restriction; Trove is not affiliated with 7-Zip, Igor Pavlov or RARLAB), through its own COM interop. It has a Windows 11 (Fluent) look that follows light/dark mode and the accent colour. It opens ZIP, 7Z, RAR and RAR5 (including encrypted and multi-part), TAR, GZ, BZ2, XZ, ZST, ISO, CAB, WIM, DMG and many other formats the 7-Zip engine reads, plus split (.001) and self-extracting archives. It creates ZIP, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ and TAR.XZ, never RAR (the format is proprietary and the unRAR licence forbids it), with Store/Fastest/Balanced/Smallest levels (7-Zip levels 0/1/5/9), AES-256 passwords for ZIP and 7Z, hidden file names for 7Z, and split parts. Extraction blocks zip-slip entries (.., absolute paths, drive letters, paths through junctions), never creates links or alternate data streams, writes each file to a temporary part until 7-Zip reports it OK, never overwrites silently, and copies the Mark of the Web from downloaded archives. Setup can add a Trove submenu to File Explorer's right-click menu (on Windows 11 under "Show more options"). Version 1.0.0 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). It updates itself: about 10 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/trove.json (nothing else is sent), and Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256 and installs it silently. 85 engine tests pass on .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8. The still images of Trove on this site are real screenshots with demo files; the 74-second launch video on the article (English captions) recreates Trove’s interface from its source. The ARM64 build was not run on ARM hardware, no build was run on an actual Windows 7 or 8.1 machine, and the all-users installation was not tested.

Inkwell is Muhammad Noman's free word processor for Windows ("Write beautifully. Without fighting your document."), written in C# with WPF, with its own layout engine on WPF's TextFormatter (its own pagination with columns, keep-with-next, widow and orphan control, tables across pages, footnotes and floating pictures, and incremental relayout). It has a Windows 11 (Fluent) look with no ribbon: a command bar that shortens in whole steps on narrow windows, an outline pane, a contextual panel (Format, Picture or Table, then Page, Review, Reveal and Design), a menu (Alt+F), a command palette (Ctrl+K) and a slash menu. It opens and saves .docx (and .docm, .dotx, .dotm) directly: saving starts from the original package, so parts it does not edit (macros, charts, SmartArt, custom XML, embedded objects) stay byte for byte, and it says so when such a file opens; text boxes are shown but not edited, charts and SmartArt are labelled placeholders, equations show as plain text, and Word 97-2003 .doc files are not supported. Nine documents saved by Inkwell 1.0.0 opened in Microsoft Word (Microsoft 365) without repairs, and Word's counts matched Inkwell's in 116 of 117 values (the sample résumé is two pages in Inkwell and one in Word). It has 8 templates, 6 designs and 11 bundled font families under the SIL Open Font License (Literata, Source Serif 4, Inter, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, DM Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono, Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto Nastaliq Urdu), embedded in saved documents by default. The start screen's tour lists twelve fixes: pictures that stay put (wrap choices with a live preview, guides, a draggable anchor, Lock position), lists that number as expected (Restart at 1, Continue from the list above, Start at...), paste that matches the document (with a chip and Ctrl+Shift+V for plain text), Reveal formatting (Shift+F1) and a style consistency check, visible labelled breaks and no stray blank last page, tables that cooperate, autocorrect and Markdown shortcuts each undone by one Ctrl+Z (with Undo / Stop doing this, and a switch for every rule in Settings), automatic save with recovery copies and version history, one landscape page in one click, click-to-edit headers and footers, a small set of styles, and live word counts. It also has tables of contents, footnotes and endnotes, captions and cross-references, bookmarks, citations (APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago 17 author-date, IEEE) with a bibliography stored in the .docx sources part, comments with replies, track changes (Ctrl+Shift+E) with four views, find and replace with regular expressions, Windows spell checking (Windows 8 and later), focus mode, typewriter scrolling, a pageless view and a word goal. Typing Urdu or Arabic in an empty paragraph turns it right to left, with Noto Nastaliq Urdu or Noto Naskh Arabic. It opens Markdown, text, RTF, ODT/FODT and HTML, exports (Ctrl+Shift+X) PDF (text as outlines with an invisible, searchable text layer in Inter and Noto Naskh Arabic, bookmarks and links), Markdown, HTML and plain text, and prints through Windows. It uses the Open XML SDK, PDFsharp (both MIT) and Markdig (BSD-2-Clause); no licence has been chosen for Inkwell itself. Version 1.0.1 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8); they are not code-signed, and setup adds Inkwell only to the Open with list for .docx and .md, never as the default app. 1.0.1 came out the same day as 1.0.0 with fixes: Ctrl+Shift+E for track changes and Ctrl+Shift+X for Export, every autocorrect rule in Settings, a command bar that never cuts a label off, and updates for installations in any folder. Its only network use is the update check: about 10 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/inkwell.json (nothing else is sent), and Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256 and installs it silently. 344 tests pass on .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8 (the engine, plus the app's shortcuts, updater and settings); on the author's PC, with 1.0.0, a 301-page, 112,562-word document loaded in 82 ms and laid out in 2.6 s, with a 2.9 ms median keystroke (.NET 10). The still images of Inkwell on this site are real screenshots of version 1.0.1 with its demo documents; the 105-second launch video on the article (English captions) recreates Inkwell's interface from its source, with every page laid out and rendered by Inkwell's own engine and a few demo edits that aren't in the shipped samples. Not tested: a real printer, screen readers, East Asian input methods, spell checking outside English, ARM64 hardware, real Windows 7/8.1 PCs and 32-bit Windows 10, exported PDFs in other PDF viewers, and the 1.0.1 ARM64, 32-bit and Windows 7/8.1 installers (the 1.0.0 installer and the 1.0.1 x64 installer passed per-user install tests).

Stagecraft is Muhammad Noman's free presentation app for Windows ("Presentations that look designed. Without the effort."), written in C# with WPF. It has a Windows 11 (Fluent) look with no ribbon: a command bar, a slide rail, the canvas, a contextual properties panel and a command palette (Ctrl+K). It has 10 themes (Aurora, Editorial, Midnight, Pastel, Corporate, Mono, Gradient, Swiss, Botanical, Slate) with 3 colour variants each, 16 smart layouts, text that shrinks to fit layout boxes, balanced title wrapping, smart guides and Tidy up, and 8 bundled font families under the SIL Open Font License (Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Space Grotesk, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Source Serif 4, JetBrains Mono). Content: bar, line, pie and donut charts, tables, 1,112 Fluent UI System Icons (MIT), shapes and connectors, pictures (crop with handles or to a circle or rounded rectangle), custom gradients, shadows, group, align, lock, copy style / paste style, header and footer, find and replace (including speaker notes), spell check as you type, rulers, gridlines and guides, a slide sorter with sections and an outline view. Transitions: Fade, Push, Slide over, Zoom and Morph. Animations (new in 1.1): 12 entrance, 8 emphasis and 12 exit effects and motion paths (line, arc, circle or drawn, editable), On click / With previous / After previous, duration, delay, repeat, rewind, easing, text by paragraph, word or letter, and triggers; an animation pane with click groups and a timeline, a gallery that previews each effect on the slide, and an animation painter (Alt+Shift+C). Links (new in 1.1) on text, shapes, pictures, icons and action buttons, to web pages (http/https only), e-mail, slides and files (files open only after a confirmation; programs and scripts are never opened). Video and sound (new in 1.1), played by Windows' own media support (MP4/H.264, MP3, M4A and WAV were checked; Windows N editions need the Media Feature Pack): embedded, or linked for files over 200 MB, with poster frame, trim, start options, full screen, loop, volume, fades and sound across slides; online video cards open in the browser. The presenter view shows notes, a timer, the clock, the next slide, the current click and a slide grid, with laser, pen, highlighter, black/white screens and rehearse timings. Files: the .stagecraft format (a ZIP with JSON, saved atomically; 1.0 files are upgraded), saved automatically a few seconds after editing once a presentation has a file (on by default), plus periodic recovery copies of unsaved work; export to vector PDF with an approximate selectable text layer (in Inter) and clickable links, PNG/JPG and .pptx (checked against the Open XML schema by tests; animations, links, video and sound and the footer are written, effects PowerPoint lacks become the closest one; charts, icons, action buttons, online video cards and theme artwork become pictures, Morph becomes a fade); .pptx import reads animations, links, video and sound, skips SmartArt, other chart types, ink and embedded objects, lists what it left out or changed, and only partly follows master/layout inheritance. It uses the Open XML SDK and PDFsharp (both MIT). Version 1.1.0 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8); they are not code-signed. It updates itself: about 10 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/stagecraft.json (nothing else is sent), and Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256 and installs it silently. Its only other network use is optional: fetching an online video's picture and title once from YouTube or Vimeo when one is added. 135 engine tests pass on .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8. The still images of Stagecraft on this site are real screenshots of versions 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 with its sample decks; the 101-second launch video on the article (English captions) recreates Stagecraft’s interface from its source, with slides rendered by Stagecraft’s own engine and a few demo edits that aren’t in the shipped sample decks. Not tested: a real full-screen or two-display slide show (tested in a windowed test mode), real mouse dragging and typing, ARM64 hardware, real Windows 7/8.1 PCs, MOV/WMV/WMA files, Windows N editions, the 1.1 installers themselves (the 1.0 installers were tested) and screen readers.

Professional experience and project figures are self-reported in the owner's supplied resume, not independently verified live analytics. Conceptual project artwork is not a screenshot of a product interface. This file does not guarantee search ranking or AI-system citation.
